claims.statement: The source declares FPT/GHEC/GHES. The product reusable describes branch/tag rulesets for public Free repositories and public/private Pro/Team/Enterprise Cloud repositories; push availability varies by plan and product. The GHES else-branch uses Enterprise Cloud wording, retained as ambiguous eligibility rather than silently generalized.
Anyone with read access can view rulesets; creating/editing/deleting requires admin or edit-repository-rules permission. The non-FPT reusable also mentions insights.

Rulesets are named rule lists; the source permits up to 75 per repository and 75 organization-wide, with cross-repository organization use for Team/Enterprise plans. These limits are pinned assertions, not locally measured platform quotas.
Rulesets can grant bypass to roles such as repository administrator, specific teams or GitHub Apps; an active ruleset therefore does not alone prove rejection for all actors.

The non-GHES paragraph describes Enterprise-plan organization targeting and GHEC-only enterprise-code-rulesets enterprise targeting; its cross-product documentation link is not GHES availability evidence.
Rulesets may target branches/tags or block repository pushes across the complete fork network; their scopes are different.

Delegated push bypass is gated to GHEC/GHES>3.15: contributors request a designated reviewer’s permission for restricted content; approval permits the push, denial requires removing that content before retrying.

Branch/tag rulesets can control pushes, tag deletion/rename and conditionally enterprise metadata. They select targets with fnmatch, including recursive releases/**/*; the illustrative administrator bypass is not mandatory local policy.
Push rules apply to every push without branch targeting and restrict paths, path lengths, extensions or sizes across the fork network. Root-repository bypass grants determine fork bypass too.
Allowed path/size exceptions in the push overview are gated to FPT/GHEC and do not establish GHES availability; other type restrictions do not acquire exceptions merely from this overview.

Rulesets and classic branch protection operate together; multiple rulesets can apply while only one classic rule applies. Evaluate the combined effective rules, not presence of a single configuration.
Ruleset enforcement status can be changed without deletion; repository readers can inspect active rulesets, and metadata-format controls add capabilities beyond classic protection.
Classic-to-ruleset conversion navigation is available only under branch-protection-ruleset-conversion (FPT/GHEC or GHES>=3.23); conversion was not performed.
Active enforces on creation; Disabled does not enforce (nor conditionally evaluate); Evaluate is a non-enforcing observation mode gated to repo-rules-enterprise, not proof of active protection.
Rulesets have no priority: applicable rules aggregate, the most restrictive variant wins, and classic protection layers with them. Branch/tag applicability must be established before aggregating.

The illustrative 3-review signed ruleset plus 2-review linear classic rule and conditional 1-review no-force-push organization ruleset yields three reviews, signing and linear history with conditional force-push blocking. Those counts are example inputs, not a universal quorum.

scope: Primary reading of full pinned article and recursively included dependencies. Reviewed source statements only; no adoption or live platform verification.
